This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 17-08-2021 at about 5.30 a.m., the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HF-6053, from Kempanahalli side towards Anchepalya.

While so traveling on Kempanahalli- Anchepalya road, Kempanahalli village, Huthridurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, the rider Narasimharaju rode the said motorcycle with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle, capsize the motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to M.M. Hospital, Kunigal, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient and underwent surgery.
Earlier to the accident, he was doing labour work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kunigal Police have registered the case against the rider of the bike bearing No.KA-06-HF-6053 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.

It has admitted the issuance of Two Wheeler-Bundled policy bearing No.2312201812932700000 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of bike bearing No.KA-06-HF-6053, valid from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2024.

From 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2020 it covers the risk of third party as well as own damages and from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2024 it covers third party risk alone and from 02-06-2020 to 02-06-2024 period the said policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider.
As the alleged accident occurred on 17-08-2021, the risk of the petitioner is not covered.
Hence, the petition as against this respondent requires to be dismissed, as it is not obligated/liable to indemnify the risk of pillion rider and not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

Further it is contended that,

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and not Narasimharaju.
The said Narasimharaju was not on the wheels of motorcycle as on the date and relevant time of accident.

The petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and owner of the vehicle/first respondent has created false crime records and story that the petitioner was pillion rider and one Narsimharaju was riding the motorcycle, to get compensation and has lodged a false complaint against the insured vehicle after lapse of several days.
As on the date of accident, the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and all the MLC records of the petitioner clearly establishes that, the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle.

The accident has occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and he was not the pillion rider on the motorcycle and he was not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner,
injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 17-08-2021 at about 5.30 a.m., due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the bike bearing registration No.KA-06- HF-6053 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award?

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motrocycle bearing Reg. No.06-HF-6053 and losing control over the said motorcycle.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.7 that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. 12. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 06-HF-6053 in the alleged accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said motorcycle and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above stated facts and circumstances of the Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/

Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and not Narasimharaju.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is representative/Senior Manager of the respondent No.2 company, there is no other corroborative evidence produced by the respondent No.2 to show that, at the relevant point of time of the accident the petitioner himself was riding the offending motorcycle due to the self rash and negligent riding he has lost control over his vehicle, fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to his self negligence and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further,
the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied all the suggestions made in his cross-examination.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 18 feet wide on Kempanahalli-Anchepalya road, near Chittemariyappa land,
Kempanahalli Village, Huthridurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending bike bearing Reg. No.06-HF-6053 and there was no other vehicle involved in the accident, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending bike bearing Reg. No.06-HF-6053.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to his self rash and negligent riding and self fall from the offending motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.06-HF-6053.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the rider of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.13 OPD records and Ex.P.14 x-rays
, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered left distal femur fracture and for the said injury he has underwent surgery.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand,
there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/

No.06-HF-6053.
15.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-08-2021 at about 5.30 a.m., on Kempanahalli-Anchepalya road, near Chittemariyappa land, Kempanahalli Village,
Huthridurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of bike bearing Reg.
No.06-HF-6053.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of bike bearing Reg. No.06-HF- 6053 and he has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained left distal femur fracture and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-06-1997.
The accident has taken place on 17-08-2021 at about 5.30 A.M. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 24 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/
6 affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left distal femur fracture and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e.
internal fixation of femur.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 30% to the left lower limb and 15% to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.13 OPD records and Ex.P.14 x-rays also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above injury and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 16-01-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 17-08- 2021, which is after lapse of two years and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, after union of the fracture the implants are removed and the restrictions of movements present at the time of surgery were improved at the time of assessment of disability.
Further he has admitted that, after removal of implants, the doctors of MM Multi-Specialty Hospital have declared the petitioner is fit for discharge.
Further, the has admitted that, the petitioner can do table works and he had come to his hospital without any support to walk.

Therefore, in such circumstances, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him,
avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record,
this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing labour work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing labour work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2021.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,80,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 24 years is 18.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 42 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,69,461/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,69,461/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., left distal femur fracture and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. internal fixation of femur.

As per Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days from 17-08-2021 to 25- 08-2021 and 09-09-2023 to 11-09-2023, in M.M.
Multispeciality Hospital, Kunigal.
He has also undergone surgery i.e. ORIF with LCP-distal femur and screws combined spinal and epidural anaesthesia.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days in M.M. Multispeciality Hospital, Kunigal.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 12 = Rs.12,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days in M.M. Multispeciality Hospital, Kunigal.
He might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.
800 x 12 = Rs.9,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Madugonahalli Village, Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakuru District, the accident has taken place on Kempanahalli-Anchepalya road, near Chittemariyappa land, Kempanahalli Village, Huthridurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk and he has taken treatment at M.M. Multispeciality Hospital, Kunigal.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 12 days as inpatient at M.M. Multispeciality Hospital, Kunigal, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore,
Rs.15,000 x 2 = Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 24 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/
8
bearing bones.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injury sustained by him in the said accident.
Even, the P.W.2 has not stated anything with respect to same.
The P.W.2 in his cross-examination has admitted that, after union of the fracture, the implants were removed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,24,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,69,461-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 12,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 9,600-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,10,061/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
As per Ex.R.1 insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HF-6053, the policy was in force, as on the date of accident.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-06-HF- 6053 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/
9 21.

But, the respondent No.2 has taken a specific contention that, as on the date of accident the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the Ex.R.1 insurance policy bearing No.2312201812932700000, issued in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HF-6053, was valid from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2024.

The said policy covers the risk of third party as well as own damage in between the period from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2020 and it covers third party risk alone in between the period from 03-06- 2019 to 02-06-2024.
Further it is contended that, in between the period from 02-06-2020 to 02-06-2024 the said policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider.
As the accident in question has occurred on 17-08-2021, the risk of petitioner is not covered under the said policy.

Hence, the petition as against the respondent No.2 requires to be dismissed, as it is not obligated/liable to indemnify the risk of pillion rider and not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

22. In view of above specific contentions taken by the respondent No.2 insurance company, the burden was on the respondent No.1/owner of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-06-HF-6053 to prove that, as on the date of accident the rider of his vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending motorcycle and the Ex.R.1 insurance policy covers the risk of pillion rider.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to discharge his burden in the instant case, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.R.1 insurance policy, it clearly reveals that, said policy covers the risk of third party as well as own damage in between the period from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2020 and it covers third party risk alone in between the period from 03-06- 2019 to 02-06-2024.
This clearly goes to show that, the said policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider in between the period from 02-06-2020 to 02-06-2024.

23. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and there is breach of fundamental condition of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, for any liability or compensation awarded by this Court.

Further argued that, as the Ex.R.1 insurance policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider of insured vehicle, in between the period from 02-06-2020 to 02-06- 2024 and as the accident in question has occurred on 17-08- 2021, the risk of petitioner is not covered under the said policy.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the risk of pillion rider and not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

24. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, the pillion rider is covered under third-party liability and as the Ex.R.1 insurance policy covers the third party risk in between the period from 03-06-2019 to 02-06-2024, the respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1 and pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Further argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act.

25. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.174/2018 (MV-D) C/w MFA No.6621/2018 (MV-D), in between The National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sanaulla Khan and others, has clearly held Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87284039/
10

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Sanaulla Khan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, "pillion rider is not covered when it is the 'Act only policy' (Liability only Policy) and no extra premium was collected for covering the risk of the pillion rider, the pillion rider or occupant of the car cannot come within the purview of the 'Third Party'.
The insurance company is not liable to pay compensation, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation."

26. As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1, there is no document placed on record by the petitioner to show that, as on the date of accident the rider of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the offending motorcycle.

Further, as per Ex.R.1 insurance policy, the third party risk alone was covered in between the period from 03-06-2019 to 02-06- 2024 and it does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider in between the said period.

As the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle had consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid & effective driving licence to ride his motorcycle and committed breach of fundamental conditions of the policy and the Ex.R.1 insurance policy does not cover the risk of occupant/pillion rider as on the date of accident, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, as the accident in question has taken place after the date of coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured, does not hold good.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, as there is breach of fundamental condition of the insurance policy by the respondent No.1 and as on the date of accident the risk of occupant/pillion rider was not covered by the Ex.R.1 insurance policy, issued in respect of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-06-HF-6053, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, holding that the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount Rs.6,10,061/- to the petitioner,
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,10,061/- (Rupees six lakh ten thousand and sixty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the same within two months from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with Prajwal Kumar .K vs Hanume Gowda on 8 April, 2025

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
